1.verdict:
VERDICT: REDO

1. **The strike is decided by a conditional, so the claim fails.** Violated: policy, "a reserved call waits on him", and §2.10, "nothing is built on it until he rules". The closing lines say a strike called before latch "ends a running breakout with the lab lost", and after latch "ends only the lab: the nodes stand". Those lines build on the placeholder and pre-decide §2.9 Q2's consequences. They contradict "Everything else in this section is the dive" and "no path that wakes the lab avoids it". They also leave a lifted drive unresolved, against *"one or the other"* (2026-10-12). Delete them. The other strike references hold.

2. **Failure can be dodged by shutting seals early.** Violated: *"Then a chance to recover or fail"* (2026-10-10). Nothing limits relays to after the breakout starts. The crew can shut seals, then pick, so every specimen is "behind a shut seal" at once. Recovery is then instant and the window is moot.

3. **The stop condition contradicts itself.** "killing or sealing everything afterwards is the road to stopping the spread" conflicts with "stops... only when every node is cleared and every specimen left in the lab is dead". Sealing is either enough or it isn't.

4. **Tank counts don't agree.**
   - Hold: 2 of 4 cells fail, so 2 remain intact. "if the crew killed every specimen" therefore can't yield the Shattered Lab unless intact tanks are killable, which is unstated. It also conflicts with "alive under seal for good". "Both stay possible all game" is unproven after a failure under Hold.
   - Take: "the rest held" conflicts with 3 of 4 failing plus 1 drawn, which leaves none held.

5. **Sealed states have no outcome.** "every pick leaves it obtainable" fails if Hold or Take seals the core with the drive still in its bay. Reopening a seal is undefined, yet post-failure clearing of sealed specimens requires it.

6. **The node rules conflict on buildability.** "generates no map layout" conflicts with "cleared by assault". RimWorld 1.6 needs a generated map to assault a site, so the spec must name a fixed authored layout or say how the clear happens.

2.verdict:
VERDICT: REDO

1. **The strike claim does not hold: one line decides part of it.** "No path that wakes the lab avoids it" and "A crew that walks away from the lab therefore still gets a breakout" are unconditional once the lab is woken. The placeholder says the strike has "no breakout", and §2.9 q2 leaves open whether it can be called after going in. Together, these lines already answer that for a strike called during the 15-day clock. "The originals stay alive under seal for good" and "the threat is over for good" also assume no later strike. All of these lines need scoping to "unless §2.9 q2/q5 rule otherwise". Violated: "a reserved call waits on him"; §2.10 "nothing is built on it".

2. **The severity ruling collapses in play.** Violated: *"Breakout always starts; choice sets how bad"* (2026-10-12). The cells start in the core, and the first seal is at the core boundary. Relays are dead until the breakout, but nothing stops a pawn waiting at one. Once the clock runs out, that pawn holds the relay for one work period, and all four specimens are behind a shut seal. Recover then fires, the purge kills them all, and the seals can be reopened to reach the drive. So the "worst breakout" costs no fight, and it is safer than any console pick. It also ends "over for good" without Burn's burnt-out core. Cell counts and windows stop mattering, and *"a chance to recover or fail"* is no chance. The design needs a seal time or a specimen head start that can't be beaten this way.

3. **State with no outcome: lifting the drive after a pick.** Trigger 2 covers only "no choice made". The console text says "If it is removed, the stasis fails." Only Hold cross-feeds the core to the stasis, and Take a specimen relies on that feed without the table saying so. Under Burn or Loose, the cells that did not fail "stay shut... still in stasis" with nothing stated to power them once the drive is gone. They may or may not fail, and the "every pick leaves it obtainable" line does not settle it.

4. **Contradiction with §2.3 and §2.5.** The build notes say bans keep Assailants out of the lab's ordinary spawn before the breakout. The owner-ruled roster has `AA_BlackDefiler`, "The Assailant's flesh", and the pale turrets, "the Assailant's OWN emplacements", online at thaw. The "mechanoid guardians" also appear nowhere in that roster.

3.verdict:
VERDICT: REDO

**1. Relays make the lab unreachable, which breaks the section's own guarantees.**
- Violated (§2.10 Recover): *"seals may be reopened afterwards… so the drive stays reachable in every end state."*
- Violated (§2.10 push-back): *"Both stay possible all game."*
- The relay *"stands on the breakout's side of its seal"*, a seal is *"reopened the same way"*, and *"a shut seal stops everything behind it."* So only a pawn inside can reopen it.
- If the shutter dies or is downed, the crew outside has no way in. The drive can't be reached, and after a failure the specimens left inside can't be killed. Nothing in the section covers this. It also doesn't say how a shutter leaves, or whether the purge hits pawns sealed in.

**2. The window doesn't work as a pawn pace, and the check is defined twice.**
- Violated (§2.10): the window *"is the lead specimen's pace."* A live pawn crosses a RimWorld map in hours, not 2–5 days, and nothing throttles it.
- With that pace, *"reaches the outer gate"* and *"the window closes"* become one event, listed as two fail conditions. If pace is real, the window never matters.
- *"Holding it takes longer than a specimen takes to cross a band"* then makes hold time the value that decides whether recovery is possible, and it has no number. It needs a stated throttle and a hold time.

**3. Held Lab has a state with no outcome.**
- Violated (§2.10 Hold row): *"The originals stay alive under seal for good"* and *"The price of keeping the records."*
- Recovery lets seals reopen, and stasis cells can be opened to kill what's inside. Killing them after the latch has no stated result: does it become the Shattered Lab, and does the Imperial attempt still come? If it does become Shattered, the records are kept and the price is dodged. The pre-latch line already does this, which beats Burn.

**4. Second escapee is undefined.**
- Only the first specimen at the gate *"is that node."* Later specimens reaching the gate have no stated result.
- If they leave, *"every specimen left in the lab is dead"* can be met by letting them walk out.

**Not defects:**
- **Rulings:** I found no contradiction or reinterpretation of any ruling.
- **Strike isolation holds:** no other line decides the strike or depends on the placeholder. *"The strike is the branch that loses it"* is the ruling's *"lab lost"*, and the closing scope line covers every "always", "for good" and "no path".

4.verdict:
VERDICT: REDO

1. **New ruling contradiction:** “Whether the strike can still be called after going in stays §2.9 question 2, unanswered here,” followed by limiting guarantees to “the dive with no strike called.” §2.6 already rules **“strike OR dive, never both.”** Treating a strike after entry as unresolved reopens an excluded combination and makes the dive’s guarantees conditional on it. Apply the existing mutual exclusion throughout.

2. **(a) Fixed:** “Every seal works from either side,” “a pawn shut in can always open its way out,” and the purge kills “every pawn, crew included.” These define access after the shutter’s death, the shutter’s escape, and the consequence of remaining inside. Opening a seal cancels the pending purge. No remaining violation found.

3. **(b) Fixed:** “A released specimen stays in the band it is in for W/3,” and shutting requires “8 in-game hours of work.” These supply the throttle and hold time. “The window is that moment, not a second condition” removes the duplicated deadline; combat explicitly modifies the schedule. No remaining violation found.

4. **(c) Fixed:** “When the last held specimen dies, at any time and by any hand, the feed burns out and takes the archive and the seated core with it.” The text also covers killing every original before recovery and preserves the owed Imperial attempt. Killing the originals no longer preserves the archive while cancelling the stated price. Previously learned knowledge surviving is an explicit allowance.

5. **(d) Fixed:** “Any specimen that reaches the gate after that opens the next listed site at once, ahead of the season.” This defines the second escape’s consequence; the later exhaustion and saturation rules cover a full site list. No remaining violation found.
4.after: round-3 gaps (a)-(d) judged fixed. The one new finding (late-strike carve-out vs "strike OR dive, never both") was fixed after the round: the dive begins at the wake and no strike follows it (§2.3, §2.9 q2, §2.10). That fix has had no judge; no fifth round run, per the brief.

Judged: design/Jawa/worldbuilding/dungeons_arc_spec.md at 2f3b549b13, §2.10 (lines 364-563), §2.9 (352-362), and the §2.3 strike bullet (178-180) the fix points to. Round 4's findings 2-5 are not reopened.

1. **The round-4 defect is narrowed, not fixed.** His ruling, as §2.6 quotes the ledger (line 278-279): *"one or the other — strike (full Cathedral trust, lab lost) OR go in and defy the Cathedral."* The alternative to the strike is "go in", not "wake". The fix redefines the dive as starting at the wake (gate 4) and leaves a strike after going in open. That is the exact case round 4 flagged ("Treating a strike after entry as unresolved reopens an excluded combination"). At gate 3 the codes open the door and "the crew stands in the approach band" (line 165), so the crew has gone in. Lines at fault:
   - §2.10 lines 538-539: "Whether a strike can be called after the door opens but before the wake is §2.9 question 2; such a strike ends the lab before any of this starts."
   - §2.3 lines 179-180: "Whether one can follow gate 3 (door open, lab not woken) stays §2.9 question 2."
   - §2.10 lines 377-378 restate the fix as "the dive begins at the wake; no strike after it".
   "Dive = the wake" is the agent's definition. His words make "go in" the branch point.

2. **§2.9 question 2 now contradicts both his ruling and §2.10.** Line 357: "can the player go in first and call the strike later? Only up to the wake". (a) Read as an answer, it allows going in and then striking, which is the "both" his "one or the other ... OR go in" excludes. (b) It is written as settled ("Only up to the wake"), in a section headed "Nothing below is ruled". Meanwhile §2.3 and §2.10 say the same window "stays §2.9 question 2", so it is still open. The three places disagree on whether the door-open, pre-wake window is open or answered.

3. **Mechanics note for the redo (not a separate defect).** If "going in" is placed at the door, Route 6 must be handled. Route 6 opens the door "without action" (line 172-173), so an opened door cannot by itself mean the player chose to go in. A consistent fix places the point of no return at the player's own act: using the codes at gate 3, or under Route 6 a crew pawn entering the approach band. Wherever it is placed, write the same thing in §2.3, §2.9 question 2 and §2.10, in line with "strike OR go in", and do not leave it as an open question. Alternatively, put "is going in the door or the wake?" to him as a question card, without §2.9 pre-answering it.

Otherwise the fix is clean. Line 394 ("The strike has none"), line 403 ("never wakes the lab ... has not made the dive"), line 417, §2.9 question 5 (line 360) and the strike paragraph (lines 531-537) are consistent with "strike ends it, no breakout". No new hole was found in the breakout, seal, recovery or spread mechanics. Trigger 2 (lifting the drive) cannot come before the wake, because the core opens only at gate 4.

6.verdict:
VERDICT: KEEP

I found no game state without an outcome, no contradiction of rulings 1–6, and no exploit that lets a player skip a choice's stated price. The notes below are minor.

1. **Ruling compliance holds.** *"On the dive it always starts: no path that wakes the lab avoids it"* together with the three triggers (choice, drive lifted, 15-day decay) satisfies ruling 2's "Breakout always starts". *"Each sets how bad the breakout is, never whether it comes"* matches "choice sets how bad". The strike paragraph (*"no choice, no breakout, no recovery and no reinfection, and the drive is lost"*) matches rulings 3 and 4. The cutoff (*"A strike can be called up to the wake… Seating the core is the point of no return"*) matches ruling 6 and agrees word for word with the §2.3 bullet and §2.9 Q2. The five choices, the breakout and recover/fail at the seals are left as ruled (ruling 5).

2. **Failure meets ruling 2's wording.** *"the second and third open in the next two seasons whatever has been cleared by then"* guarantees spread over seasons. *"the peak reached is a floor… every failure leaves at least +5% for good"* guarantees "game continues harder". There is no win or lose state, so G14 holds. The spread comes from a fixed list and only adds or removes sites, so it does not break the no-worldgen rule.

3. **No way to dodge a price.** For Hold, killing the originals burns the records and the Imperial attempt *"is still owed"*. Seals cannot be pre-shut because *"relays are dead until the breakout starts"*. Lifting the drive after a pick changes nothing, and before a pick it counts as Leave them. Walking away still fails, both by the clock and by leaving with a specimen loose. Each choice's stated cost survives.

4. **Minor: unfailed cells and the purge.** *"fires through every sealed band, in the cells and out of them"*. Under Burn the cells (1 of 4 fails) or Loose the experiments (2 of 4), the crew can meet the check by killing every released specimen in the core without shutting any bulkhead, because unfailed cells "count as sealed". It is then unclear whether the core is a "sealed band" the purge reaches. If it is not, live originals sit in stasis on the reactor while the result table says *"the originals are dead"* (Shattered Lab, Feeding Lab). "In the cells" probably covers this, but one clause saying the purge always reaches the unfailed cells would close it.

5. **Minor: Hold or Take a specimen after a failure.** *"Sealing alone stops nothing after a failure… no purge or stasis comes to settle it."* This leaves unsaid whether the core feed and the archive keep running for held specimens once failure latches. That includes failure from the Imperial attempt, which by definition comes after the feed had already re-stased them. The game is not left without an outcome: specimens remain killable, and the list's stop condition (*"every specimen left in the lab is dead"*) is defined. Only the archive's fate is open.

6. **Minor: an outcome stated for recovery only.** *"so the drive stays reachable in every end state"* comes under Recover. After a failure the drive can in practice still be reached, since seals open from either side and specimens can be killed, so nothing breaks. The section just doesn't say so.

7. **Minor: an unstated assumption.** *"Every open node adds 5%… the peak reached is a floor"*, together with *"The first opens the moment failure latches"*, gives the +5% minimum. That minimum depends on at least one node always opening on failure, which the text guarantees; it is worth keeping that link if the build changes when nodes open.

None of these is a ruling contradiction or a game state without an outcome. Notes 4 and 5 are one-line clarifications the build item (`WARLAB_BREAKOUT_BUILD_SEALS_HOLD_THE_LINE`) can absorb.
6.after: minor notes 4-5 (purge reach into unfailed cells; feed and archive after a failure under Hold/Take) left to WARLAB_BREAKOUT_BUILD_SEALS_HOLD_THE_LINE

rounds.1:
VERDICT: REDO

1. **The strike exemption reinterprets the ruling.** “Breakout always starts; choice sets how bad” (§2.1, owner, 2026-10-12) becomes “governs the dive” in §2.10. “Destroy them once and for all” (§2.6) establishes the strike’s result, not whether a breakout precedes destruction. Delegation permits application but forbids “reinterpret[ing] what a ruling says” (canon_excerpt.md). This exemption needs an owner ruling.

2. **Recovery does not produce the promised aftermath.** Recovery permits every specimen to be “behind a shut seal” (§2.10), yet recovered Burn, Loose, and Leave declare the originals dead. Sealing living originals satisfies recovery without killing them. Those planetary outcomes therefore do not follow from the mechanics.

3. **Failure lacks explicit precedence over recovery.** “Any specimen reaches the outer gate unsealed” causes failure, but subsequent killing or sealing can satisfy recovery “sooner” (§2.10). Recovery then promises “Nothing spreads.” Specify that failure latches permanently; otherwise later containment can erase the owner’s consequence: “If containment fails → Reinfection spreads” (§2.1).

4. **The casket has no defined place in the outcome check.** “Every live specimen is dead or behind a shut seal” (§2.10) does not cover a living specimen carried outside in a sealed casket. Explicitly exempt or classify it; otherwise the intended Take recovery cannot satisfy the written predicate.

5. **Permanent difficulty contradicts the stated raid mechanism.** “The threat level never falls back below the level the failure reached,” but raids are “scaled by the count of open nodes” (§2.10). Clearing every node removes every stated raid source. Define the lasting consequence that fulfills “game continues harder” (§2.1, owner ruling).

6. **Failure text can state something false.** “UI text states facts dry” (canon_excerpt.md), yet “A specimen has left the complex” also accompanies timeout or departure failures with specimens still inside.

7. **No RimWorld 1.6 impossibility is established.** The missing PawnKindDef, off-map persistence, seals, and site interception remain implementation debts. Their absence warrants verification, not an unsupported declaration that the design is unbuildable.
rounds.2:
VERDICT: REDO

1. **Strike ruling: permissible delegated application.** On the supplied record, the strike is a case the breakout ruling does not name. “Specimen choice vs breakout” and the earlier specimens card govern handling the specimens during the dive. The separate ruling permits “strike (full Cathedral trust, lab lost)” (§2.6). Reading these together supports the exemption. The revenge motive alone would not establish it, but the recorded question and separate branch do. This does **not** change what the breakout ruling says.

2. **REDO — failure can evade its consequences.** Constraint: “failure = reinfection spreads from the lake across the world over seasons, game continues harder” (owner, 2026-10-12, quoted §2.1). Leave with specimens loose, then return and kill them before the first seasonal node: §2.10 permits new nodes to stop permanently, with no guaranteed initial node and potentially a zero threat floor. Escaped originals also have no explicit continuing role in spread. Specify an unavoidable spread consequence when failure latches and how escaped sources are resolved.

3. **REDO — one recovery outcome lacks a valid transition.** Constraint: specify “what ‘recover’ and ‘fail’ each leave behind on the planet” (user’s item criteria). Under **Loose the experiments**, all experiments can die fighting specimens or crew. Sealing surviving originals nevertheless satisfies Recover. The promised resolution—“the experiments finish it”—then has no surviving actor, while the outcome table declares the originals dead and experiments loose. Define the outcome when experiments die before completing their task.

4. **Coverage and buildability:** The choices, three triggers, and intended planetary outcomes are otherwise explicit. No inherent RimWorld 1.6 impossibility is established. Persistent scheduling has an implementation precedent in [VEF’s world-component source](https://github.com/notfood/RimWorld-VanillaExpandedFramework/blob/main/Source/VEF/Factions/GameComponents/WorldComponent_FactionGoodwillImpactManager.cs). The missing PawnKindDef, unloaded-map resolution, and seal behavior remain unverified build dependencies; “not built” alone does not establish “unbuildable.”
rounds.3:
VERDICT: REDO

1. **The strike exception reinterprets the breakout ruling.** Constraint: “Breakout always starts; choice sets how bad” (owner, §2.1, `WARLAB_SPECIMENS_DESIGN_BREAKOUT_CHOICE`). §2.10 explicitly narrows this to the dive. The strike ruling promises destruction, but does not explicitly exempt it from a breakout preceding destruction. Delegation says agents “may NOT overturn or reinterpret what a ruling says” (`canon_excerpt.md`). The exemption needs owner resolution.

2. **Failure can bypass the required seasonal spread.** Constraint: “failure = reinfection spreads from the lake across the world over seasons, game continues harder” (owner, §2.1). Let one specimen escape, then kill every specimen remaining inside: new nodes stop permanently, even while the escaped node remains active. If every specimen escapes, the stopping condition is already satisfied. Failure can therefore produce one node and a permanent +5% modifier without any seasonal expansion. This also conflicts with the independently replicating scouts described in §2.1, card 5.

3. **Some recoveries have contradictory planetary outcomes.** Constraint: specify “what ‘recover’ and ‘fail’ each leave behind on the planet” (user’s item criteria). Recovery permits every live specimen to be dead. Yet Hold them and Take a specimen always produce a Held Lab with living originals and a possible Imperial release. Killing all remaining originals satisfies recovery but contradicts that outcome. The aftermath must distinguish survivors from extermination.

4. **The conditional late strike can erase an established failure.** Constraint: “If containment fails → Reinfection spreads” (owner, §2.1). Calling a strike after a specimen escapes cannot simply classify the running breakout as recovery: an external node already exists. The paragraph needs to preserve established reinfection and its consequences.

5. **No intrinsic RimWorld 1.6 impossibility is demonstrated.** The missing PawnKindDef and unloaded-map resolution are unresolved implementation dependencies. §2.7’s prohibition on custom C# specifically governs the thaw trigger; it does not establish that the entire breakout system must use vanilla quest nodes.
rounds.4:
VERDICT: REDO

1. **REDO — the spread eventually has no defined next state.** §2.10 requires: “While either remains, a new node opens each season,” using a “fixed, hand-authored list of sites,” while cleared nodes stay cleared. Leave one specimen alive in the lab and clear each node as it appears: eventually the finite list is exhausted, yet the termination condition remains false. There is no saturation rule or eligible next destination. This fails the requested check for “logical holes (a state with no outcome…)” (task). The governing owner consequence is “failure = reinfection spreads from the lake across the world over seasons, game continues harder” (§2.1, owner ruling 2026-10-12); the implementation needs a defined outcome when destinations run out.

2. **The dive otherwise follows the quoted sequence.** Specimen choices, three breakout triggers, severity differences, recovery conditions and planetary aftermath are explicit. Walking away after waking the lab still produces breakout and failure. Failure guarantees spread over multiple seasons and permanently harder raids; eventual suppression does not erase those consequences. No direct contradiction or prohibited reinterpretation of the quoted owner rulings is apparent here.

3. **No inherent RimWorld 1.6 impossibility is demonstrated.** The missing live PawnKindDef and persistent breakout, site and raid logic remain implementation dependencies. The text does not establish that existing quest nodes alone implement them, but §2.7’s explicit no-custom-C# ruling concerns the thaw trigger; extending that prohibition to the whole breakout would itself require justification.
rounds.5:
VERDICT: KEEP

1. **The dive answers the required questions.** Five specimen choices have distinct costs and severity. Console completion, drive removal, or post-thaw decay starts the breakout. Recovery specifies the surviving lab state; failure produces planetary reinfection over seasons.

2. **“Breakout always starts; choice sets how bad” is preserved** (owner, 2026-10-12, §2.1). Even Burn releases live originals. Taking the drive defaults to the worst breakout. Abandoning an awakened lab still runs the countdown and unattended failure. No stated dive route avoids the breakout.

3. **The recovery opportunity follows the breakout**, matching “Then there is the start of a breakout. Then a chance to recover or fail” (owner, 2026-10-10, §2.1). Killing or sealing specimens resolves recovery; escape, timeout, or departure with loose specimens latches failure. Later cleanup cannot retroactively erase failure.

4. **Failure satisfies the planetary consequence.** The immediate node and guaranteed second and third seasonal nodes prevent quick cleanup from cancelling “reinfection spreads … over seasons, game continues harder” (owner ruling, §2.1). The permanent threat floor preserves a lasting consequence. Eventual containment is delegated recovery detail; the ruling does not require endless, unstoppable spread.

5. **The inventions remain within the stated delegation.** Hyperdrive-powered stasis, choice costs, seals, casket benefits, and surviving lab states supply mechanics the owner left open. The quoted rulings do not require recovery to kill every original.

6. **No demonstrated RimWorld 1.6 impossibility is established.** The missing PawnKindDef and deferred persistence, seal, and spread implementation remain build dependencies. They warrant implementation verification, but do not alone justify declaring the design unbuildable. Section 2.7’s explicit vanilla-node restriction governs the thaw trigger; it does not expressly impose that restriction on every §2.10 mechanic.
